# Installed mobile app: build rules

Apply these rules while you build. Domains or criteria whose `applies_if` flags are false in `.quality/project.json` do not apply to this project. Before you call a task done, check your work against the criteria of the domains you touched: each one must be true and verifiable.

If a stack module of the quality pack is installed (qp-nextjs, qp-node-api, qp-vps, qp-expo, qp-capacitor), its rules skill adds stack-specific rules on top of these.

## Native mobile experience (MUX)

Key tasks played on a device, platform rules, keyboard, safe areas, offline, notifications.

Applies when: Installed mobile app (App Store, Google Play).

Rules:

- Choose the approach before the code and write it down: PWA, Capacitor (wrapping the web app), Expo/React Native, Flutter. A bare website wrapper is refused by Apple.
- Give a stable identifier (testID, accessibilityIdentifier, resource-id) to every element a key task touches: tests and screen readers depend on it.
- Touch targets: 44 × 44 pt on iOS, 48 × 48 dp spaced by 8 dp on Android.
- Respect safe areas and edge-to-edge display (mandatory on Android when targeting API 36); the focused field and the main action stay visible with the keyboard open.
- Follow the platform's habits: back (iOS gesture, Android button with predictive back), tab bar for navigation and not for actions, sheets dismissed by swiping.
- Text enlarged up to 200 %, dark theme, rotation and tablet: nothing is clipped or overlapping.
- Offline: write down, per kind of data, what can be read without network and what happens to a write (refused, queued, synced later with a conflict rule).
- Notifications: never ask for permission on first launch; ask after a user action, with a screen that says why.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] MUX-01: Every key task completes on a device or an emulator. Check: mobile.json: every flow of project.json › mobile.flows completed, on Android and, when a Mac is available, on iOS. Say which platforms were played.
- [major] MUX-02: Touch targets at platform sizes. Check: On the flow screenshots: no target under 44 × 44 pt (iOS) or 48 × 48 dp (Android) among the key-task actions.
- [major] MUX-03: Keyboard, safe areas and edge-to-edge. Check: Screenshots with the keyboard open: field and submit button visible. No control under the status bar, the notch, the home indicator or the gesture bar.
- [major] MUX-04: Back, tabs and sheets follow the platform. Check: Back returns to the previous screen and loses no input without warning; the tab bar is for navigation, with no overflow "More" tab; a sheet closes by swiping.
- [major] MUX-05: Text at 200 %, dark theme and tablet without breakage. Check: Screenshots at the largest font size, in dark theme and on a screen of 600 dp or more: no clipped text, no hard-coded white surface, no forced portrait.
- [major] MUX-06: Offline behaviour written and kept. Check: A flow goes offline (offline step): cached content readable, clear message, no data lost after closing and reopening the app online.
- [major] MUX-07: Permissions asked at the right time. Check: No request on first launch; each request follows an action and an explanation screen; a refusal does not block the app; one setting per kind of notification.
- [major] MUX-08: Every element has a name for VoiceOver and TalkBack. Check: Key-task controls: accessible name, role and state exposed; decorative images hidden; every gesture has a single-tap alternative.
- [minor] MUX-09: Cold start under 2 seconds on a mid-range device. Check: Android: `adb shell am start -S -W` (TotalTime). 5 seconds or more is Google Play's "excessive" line: fail.

## Store release and mobile security (MRL)

What blocks a release: API levels, privacy, account deletion, payment rules, safe storage.

Applies when: Installed mobile app (App Store, Google Play).

Rules:

- Write down at kickoff the sales model and the target storefronts: consumer sales in the app (in-app purchase required, except the United States), sales to organisations outside the app (no in-app purchase, and no purchase link in the app), or companion app without purchase.
- Account deletion: a path inside the app (Apple and Google) and a public web page (Google).
- Tokens and secrets in the Keychain (iOS) or the Keystore (Android); never in AsyncStorage, SharedPreferences, localStorage or a file.
- No secret in the shipped app: public keys only. Everything in the package can be read.
- TLS only, without exception; verified https links for authentication (no custom URL scheme); WebView restricted to the app's own origins.
- Over-the-air updates: fixes and content only; a new feature, permission or payment path goes through the store.
- Keep the list of embedded SDKs up to date: it feeds the Data safety form (Google) and the privacy labels (Apple).

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] MRL-01: No release blocker readable in the project. Check: mobile-check.json: no failed "must" (target API level, debuggable build, cleartext traffic, privacy manifest, permission texts, WebView, deletion page).
- [BLOCKER] MRL-02: Account deletion possible inside the app (only if: has_auth). Check: Path found from the settings; it deletes the account and its data (not a mere deactivation), states the delay and confirms; store subscriptions are flagged.
- [BLOCKER] MRL-03: Store payment rules met for the declared sales model (only if: has_payments). Check: project.json › mobile.monetisation and storefronts compared with the screens: in-app purchase where required; no price, subscribe button or external purchase link where forbidden.
- [BLOCKER] MRL-04: Tokens in safe storage, no secret in the shipped app. Check: Search for storage APIs in the code; search for keys in the built package (apkleaks, or unzip and search); gitleaks on the repository.
- [major] MRL-05: Store privacy forms accurate. Check: List of embedded SDKs compared with the Data safety form (Google) and the privacy labels (Apple); privacy policy link.
- [major] MRL-06: Third-party login comes with a privacy-preserving option (iOS) (only if: has_auth). Check: If the app offers Google, Facebook or another: an equivalent option limited to name and email that lets users hide their email (Sign in with Apple qualifies).
- [major] MRL-07: Links into the app verified. Check: Android: `adb shell pm get-app-links <package>` shows "verified" for each domain. iOS: the association file answers without redirect and contains the app identifier.
- [major] MRL-08: Crashes tracked, staged rollout and rollback planned. Check: Crash reporting wired in; staged rollout; rollback procedure for over-the-air updates. Google Play lines: 1.09 % crashes, 0.47 % freezes (ANR).
- [major] MRL-09: Over-the-air updates limited to fixes. Check: No over-the-air update adds a feature, a permission or a payment path; rule written in the repository.
